subject: Competitive Bake-off Recap: Redwood vs. Competitors — Acme Travel
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jackson <ajackson@acmetravel.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive Bake-off Recap: Redwood vs. Competitors — Acme Travel

Hi Alex / team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. As promised, here’s a quick recap of what we heard, the decision criteria you shared, and the proposed next steps for the competitive bake-off. I’ve included Ben and Dev to own the test plan and tech validation.

Summary of pain points (from our call):
- Booking latency spikes during flash sales (tail latency > 1s for conversational booking flow).
- High per-token inference cost with current vendor; want ~30% unit-cost reduction.
- Hallucinations on fare rules & refundable/cancellation policy answers leading to incorrect agent responses.
- Data isolation / PCI scope concerns — preference for private deployment or strict tenancy controls.

Goals and decision criteria you emphasized:
1) Latency: 95th/99th tail < 200ms for single-turn inference at target traffic patterns (we’ll replicate your peak session mix).
2) Cost: measurable token-cost reduction versus Vendor A at production-quality output.
3) Accuracy / Safety: hallucination rate on your prompt set < X% (we’ll run your prompts).
4) Security & compliance: ability to meet PCI-scope controls, SOC2 evidence, and KMS integration.
5) Ops: rollout & rollback controls, canary routing, and deterministic cost/latency dashboards.

Competitive notes (from discussion):
- Vendor A (LargeCloudAI): good managed experience but higher token costs and limited deployment isolation.
- Vendor B (OpenServe): lower cost but patchier quality and slower support for enterprise controls.

Open questions we committed to answer:
- Can Redwood hit the latency targets under your peak workload? (Ben/Dev to run bench)
- Can we match or beat Vendor A on unit economics at equivalent quality levels? (we’ll run cost-normalized tests)
- What specific evidence do you need for PCI scope and vendor onboarding? (Acme to share checklist)

Proposed bake-off plan / next steps (high level):
1) Acme shares canonical prompt set and a short evaluation rubric — we’ll run the prompts against Redwood + Vendor A/B. (You already mentioned a .xlsx; thanks.)
2) Redwood will provision a sandbox environment (hosted demo + optional dedicated test pool) and share access.
3) Ben/Dev will execute three tests: latency under synthetic peak, hallucination/accuracy eval, and cost-per-token run at production tokenization levels.
4) We’ll deliver a results deck and sample logs, plus a short live joint review.

Tentative timeline: provision sandbox by Feb 16, run tests Feb 17–20, results review week of Feb 23. Happy to adjust to your schedule.

Attachments: acme_prompt_set.txt (please confirm this is the canonical set), redwood_test_plan_v1.pdf (draft test plan / metrics).

Action items:
- Alex: confirm evaluation rubric and any additional prompts / datasets to include.
- Acme procurement: share any security checklist or PO cadence if procurement wants to be looped.
- Ben/Dev (Redwood): prepare sandbox and test harness; share access + instructions.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short calendar invite for provisioning/hand-off once we confirm times.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: acme_prompt_set.txt (text file)
Attachment: redwood_test_plan_v1.pdf (PDF stub)

Subject: Re: Competitive Bake-off Recap: Redwood vs. Competitors — Acme Travel

Marissa,

Appreciate the clear recap — this matches what we discussed. A couple quick notes:

1) I attached our evaluation criteria spreadsheet (Acme-eval-criteria.xlsx) with weighting for latency, accuracy, cost, and compliance.
2) For hallucination testing, please include at least 500 prompt variations covering edge-case fare rules and multi-leg itineraries — we can add more examples to the prompt set if helpful.
3) Procurement will need a copy of your SOC2 + any SOC2 Type II report redacted as appropriate. They also requested a short access/control diagram showing where customer data sits for hosted vs. private deployments.

Sandbox access in the week of Feb 16 works for us. If you can provision credentials and a simple runbook, we’ll start smoke tests and then run the full eval.

Thanks — look forward to the results.

Alex Jackson

ajackson@acmetravel.com | +1 617-555-0199

Looping in a quick tech checklist for the bake-off runs — keeping this thread so the customer context stays intact. Dev, can you pick these up and confirm ETA?

Tech checklist (initial):
- Provision hosted sandbox creds (read/write API key + rate limits matching Acme production sample).
- Deploy dedicated test pool (2 GPUs) for deterministic latency tests; capture 95th/99th latency and p95 token cost.
- Ingest acme_prompt_set.txt + extra 500 prompt variations (as Alex requested).
- Run hallucination eval: compare ground-truth answers to model outputs; output confusion matrix and summary metrics.
- Cost test: run a 24h cost-run at production tokenization patterns and compare unit cost vs Vendor A.
- Capture sample debug traces and KV cache stats for sharing.

Deliverables: test-results-template.csv, results deck, and raw logs (redacted). ETA for sandbox + runbook?
